text:
maria.k: Quick PSA — we discovered that older DB backups in us-west-2 are still encrypted with the legacy customer-managed key (cmk-backups-v1). Need to rotate keys, confirm restore-only RBAC, and make sure audit logs cover key usage. Can ops/security weigh in?
ajay: Agreed. What's the impact window? Are restores failing or just using an older KEK?
maria.k: No restore failures. It's a risk surface: the v1 key isn't in our rotation policy and its IAM bindings include a broader group than necessary (devs had decrypt in the past). We should
  - rotate key
  - re-encrypt snapshots if feasible
  - tighten RBAC so only backup-service and oncall role can decrypt
kevin: For re-encrypting snapshots we should prefer server-side copy if supported by the provider to avoid full download/reupload. For S3: use copy_object with SSE-KMS; for GCS maybe rewrite with new CMEK.
natalie: On RBAC: propose two new roles — backups_reader (restore-only) and backups_admin (manage keys/rotation). backups_reader should be allowed kms:Decrypt and s3:GetObject only for backup buckets/prefixes.
ajay: Sounds good. We need an audit trail requirement: all KMS:Decrypt events for backup keys must be forwarded to Splunk/Seq with 90-day retention. Also log object-copy events for re-encryption jobs.
sre-oncall: Can we schedule key rotation during low-traffic window? Also want automatic fallback in case re-encrypt job fails mid-way. We should add a circuit-breaker to stop new restores until manual approval on failure.
maria.k: Plan put together:
  1) Create cmk-backups-v2 with rotation enabled.
  2) Add kms:Encrypt to backup-service principal, kms:Decrypt to backups_reader and oncall only.
  3) Run re-encrypt job using provider-side copy, verify checksums.
  4) Update snapshot metadata to reference v2 and mark v1 deprecated for 30 days before delete.
  5) Forward KMS audit logs and object copy logs to central SIEM and create alert for any kms:Decrypt outside expected principals.
kevin: Example IAM snippet for least privilege (AWS-style):

{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cmk-backups-v2",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:ViaService": "s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com"}}
}

natalie: Also remember cross-account restore use case for customer support. We should add a short-lived assumption role flow rather than granting broad decrypt rights to the entire support org.
ajay: Vulnerability check — during vuln triage we flagged that backup-service had AWS SDK default retry set to 0 which caused partial copy failures under burst. Fix queued as PR #3842.
maria.k: Good catch. Include this in the runbook step: if re-encrypt job reports >0% failed objects, pause, notify oncall, and run integrity verify.
sre-oncall: I'll add the circuit-breaker and the PagerDuty hook. Can someone open a ticket to request Splunk ingestion for kms:Decrypt logs (source: CloudTrail) and object copy logs (source: storage access logs)?
kevin: I'll open it. Ticket: SIEM-2468. ETA for rotation dry-run: next Tue during maintenance window.
kms-bot: Scheduled rotation dry-run for cmk-backups-v2 on 1759004800 by kevin.
kms-bot: NOTE: Remember to rotate token used by re-encrypt job — do not reuse long-lived credentials.
maria.k: Thanks all. I'll draft the runbook and post the link here when ready. TL;DR: create v2, lock down RBAC, re-encrypt via server-side copy, forward logs, add circuit-breaker for restores, follow deletion delay for v1.
